variant_summary: Clear buyer-room thesis and human-agent workflow, but the scope is too broad and write controls are under-specified.
Compressed the app to one fictional buyer, six requirements, three surfaces, nine tools, and a canonical demo. Brand gate: pass. Evidence gate: ready.
Bound the stack, state model, shared domain actions, deterministic fixtures, Cloudflare deployment, and four verification layers to the canonical demo. Brand gate: pass. Evidence gate: ready.
More screens and personas improved visual breadth but weakened the demo spine and raised implementation risk. Rejected.

Added enforced proposal integrity, evidence eligibility, deterministic requirement rules, genuine activity events, security boundaries, a twelve-case eval suite, and a distinctive visual direction. Brand gate: pass. Evidence gate: ready.
Shareable rooms add identity, permissions, schema, privacy, and network failure modes without improving the canonical single-session demo.
An embedded model duplicates the browser agent, adds credentials and network risk, and makes WebMCP less central.
Sending vendor requests introduces consequential external effects and integrations. A visible unsent draft preserves the value safely.
A general evidence schema is reusable but weakens the specific buyer story and adds ingestion scope. It does not beat the 94-point best.
Real-time stakeholder collaboration has product value but requires identity, permissions, conflict handling, and backend state. It does not beat the 94-point best.
